prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on the specifics of your crash, injuries, insurance issues, and what you want (fast settlement vs. trial). I can, however, help you find a top lawyer for your situation. Below are practical steps, resources, and what to look for.

Why there’s no single “best”
- Different lawyers have different strengths (catastrophic injury/trial experience vs. frequent settlement work).  
- Case specifics (seriousness of injuries, liability disputes, uninsured motorist, multiple defendants) change which attorney is ideal.  
- Location, communication style, and fee structure matter.

Where to search and vet attorneys
- Super Lawyers and Martindale-Hubbell for peer ratings and profiles.  
- Avvo and Google/Yelp for client reviews.  
- Illinois Trial Lawyers Association and Chicago Bar Association for referrals.  
- Illinois Attorney Registration & Disciplinary Commission (ARDC) to check disciplinary history.  
- Ask for recommendations from friends, doctors, or other lawyers.

Key qualifications and red flags
- Experience: years handling car-accident claims and trial experience if your case may go to court.  
- Results: documented settlements/verdicts for similar injuries.  
- Resources: ability to retain accident reconstructionists, medical experts, and handle liens.  
- Communication: timely responses and clear explanations.  
- Local experience: familiarity with Chicago-area courts, judges, and insurers.  
- Red flags: vague answers about fees/results, poor reviews about communication, disciplinary history.

Questions to ask in the free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases like mine (type/severity of injury)? Any notable results?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?  
- What is your fee structure and what costs will I be responsible for up front?  
- How do you handle medical liens and claims by my insurer?  
- What’s your approach to settlement vs. going to trial?  
- Can you provide client references or recent verdicts/settlements?

Common fee/cost points
- Most PI lawyers work on contingency (typical contingency fee ~33% of recovery for settlement; can be higher if case goes to trial or appeal). Confirm percentages and whether costs (filing, expert fees) are deducted before/after the fee.  
- You should not pay hourly or upfront legal fees for a regular car-accident PI case.

Timing and deadlines
- Illinois statute of limitations for personal injury is normally 2 years from the accident date — act promptly. If a government entity is involved, different notice rules and shorter deadlines may apply.

Reputable Chicago firms you can consider (examples)
- Clifford Law Offices — longstanding Chicago firm with a strong reputation in major injury and car-accident litigation.  
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard — known for personal injury/medical malpractice work.  
(These are examples; you should still vet any attorney against the criteria above.)

What I can do next
- If you tell me your ZIP code and a brief summary of the crash/injuries and whether you’ve spoken to insurers, I can put together a short list of Chicago attorneys/firms that match your needs and provide contact details and recent reviews.
